description:
Stop videos from pausing when you switch tabs.

Focus Spoofer keeps the tabs you choose always active. The page always sees a visible, focused window, so TikTok, Twitch, music players and lecture videos keep playing while you work in another tab, minimize the browser or use a second monitor.

Free and open source, for Chrome, Edge and Brave. No account.

What it does
• Hides tab switches and minimizing (Page Visibility API: document.hidden stays false)
• Hides other windows and apps (hasFocus() stays true, blur never fires)
• Keeps video and animation running in background tabs, including inside embedded players
• Optional fingerprint randomization (canvas, WebGL, audio), which you can turn off in Settings

Useful for
• Streams and short videos that stop when you click away
• Music and podcast players that pause when the window loses focus
• Lecture and training videos that pause when you switch tabs
• Timers, animations and "Are you still there?" prompts that fire when you look away

How it works
Turn it on for the tab you're watching, or tick "Always protect this site" to cover it on every visit. The tab reloads once so protection starts before the site's own scripts. If a site breaks when it reloads, turn off "Reload on toggle" to switch protection on in place. Buttons, forms and menus inside the page keep working normally.

See it work: focus.oddworks.us/test
Guides: blog.oddworks.us

Private by design: no account, and your browsing history and page content never leave your browser. Optional anonymous usage stats are off unless you turn them on.

FAQ
Does it work in Edge and Brave? Yes. Install it from this page. Edge asks once to allow extensions from other stores.
Is it open source? Yes, under the Apache-2.0 license: github.com/Abhinav-ranish/Focus-Spoofer
Will it slow my browser down? No. It only runs in the tabs and sites you turn it on for.
What can't it do? It can't stop the browser from unloading a tab to save memory (Memory Saver in Chrome, sleeping tabs in Edge); for that, add the site to the browser's list of sites to keep active. It's built for desktop browsers, not phones, and it can't run on chrome:// pages or the Chrome Web Store.

What's new in 1.9.0: the store name in your language, and a welcome page that shows how to pin the extension and test it.

Email: hello@oddworks.us
